lanes.stage: mixed precision on a graphics card
lanes.summary: Moved the simulator onto the graphics card in mixed precision behind one switch for precision and device. A tune-up dropped to about six seconds with gates as good as double precision, and to 3.4 seconds on ARC's L40S cards, though every process there pays a four-minute start. Merged into main.

records.text: The coupled-block index follows the Hamiltonian's device
Tensors are made on their data's device, explicitly: making the device torch's default cost two seconds of three and a half in placement

The ramps decomposed as the coupled block in double, phases reduced, slices built and composed in the bulk precision; the pair's ramp is one summed phase. No matrix exponential and no device round trip left in placement
Decompose in chunks: the card's batched solver's workspace outgrows its memory
The levels are decomposed on the processor whatever the device: the card's batched solver wants 17 GB of workspace for 32,768 four-by-four matrices
Placement scores many operating points in one call: the grid all at once, each compass step's probes together - read in the same order and recorded up to the accepted one, so the search is unchanged
Decompose on the card in chunks of 4,096: 3.5 times the server processor's speed, and inside the solver's workspace

The simulator in mixed precision: propagators from the coupled block's levels in double, phases reduced, the rest in single, the free sequence's closing phase reduced in double; double mode keeps the matrix exponential and its gradients. The level helpers are shared with placement. Readings within 1.7e-6 of double, log-likelihoods within 1.7e-6 nats, 3.9x on the laptop's processor
The precision check runs the simulator eight devices at a time
The crowd's exact likelihood and the loop's placement run on the device numerics names; a whole-tune-up benchmark
The closed form's likelihood and the chooser's predictions run on the device numerics names; one chunked eigendecomposition in numerics for every caller; the card's likelihood chunk halved
A test that mixed precision agrees with double: readings, a log-likelihood at 2,500 shots, gate fidelities at long holds

An accurate element-wise solver for the coupled block (an arrowhead: each level as a shift from its nearest pole by a rational iteration, the exchange carried as the spin pair's centre); mixed mode uses it in double instead of the library eigensolver, and a single mode runs it in single - not yet accurate at the idle-point crossings
The coupled-block solver can be compiled into fused kernels on a card (QUAST_COMPILE=1), for comparison
On the processor the library solver serves the fast modes (faster there, exact in double); the phase ladder runs on the named device
Tests for the element-wise solver against the general one across the prior and the window; the single mode marked experimental
Both batteries in mixed precision on a card

The loop never reads a device out of memory as an unsamplable posterior: caught as one it gave zero headroom and confident stops on barely narrowed crowds when three processes shared a card. Test; the card batteries run one process at a time

lanes.summary: Barrier control: tuning the barrier gate as well as the detuning. The decisions were laid out before any code, then the exchange law was learned in 2.3 minutes a tune-up and was honest on every run. Delayed acceptance is switched off until it is shown to be unbiased, and RIKEN's measured slope and charging energy have just come in. Still open.

8br's third fast-gate defect: the headroom the stopping rule weighs scored each device at its analytic CZ time, which for a gate of a few ns is far below its best (0.73 against 0.998), so an unsettled crowd saw nothing left to gain and stopped; a known device is now credited at its CZ time moved by the crowd's own ramp shift, or the best it reached in the scans. Test fails on the previous code (headroom 0.0)

8by: RIKEN's exchange against barrier voltage (private communication via Natalia, 19 Oct) - 0.03 per mV in t_c, about 2.6x shallower than the germanium-centred prior; Reed's form fits three times better and saturation sits inside the CZ's range; the barrier range too short for silicon. Three changes proposed for Alec, none applied. Points recovered exactly from the vector PDF into references/data/ (now tracked); FINDINGS 9.10; CLAUDE.md 9 item 1 half answered; the figure's legend is per e-fold, not per decade

8bz: RIKEN's charging energy - addition voltage 50-60 mV at 80-100 µeV/mV, 4,500-5,400 µeV in our units, inside the prior; they work in (3,1), which the six-level model maps with a closed shell; their barrier sweep was at the symmetry point. The prior can represent them through the barrier (0.7-7.5 µeV of coupling over their curve); the 4.47 µeV coupling ceiling belongs on the exchange. CLAUDE.md 9 item 1 answered but for what Delta V_B is; FINDINGS 9.11; their virtualised diagram in references/data/
